sentences.text: Shri Sudarshan Joshi - Government Advocate for the respo Shri Satya Narayan Vyas, Advocate for the respondent No.3.
Considered I.A. No.6454 of 2024 , which is an application for amendment in the memo of writ petition to challenge the award dated 12.03.2024 as amended on 10.06.2024.

The award has been passed during pendency of the petition the initial challenge in which was to the proceeding under Section 11 of the The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Though the application has been opposed by learned counsel for the respondents on the ground that passing of the award is a fresh cause of action and the petitioner ought to institute a separate writ petition, but it is observed that the petition is for challenging the land acquisition proceeding.
The same has been entertained and during its pendency the final award has been passed.
The same is a subsequent event and can very well be challenged by petitioner and relegating him to prefer an independent petition for the same would only result in multiplicity of litigation.
Thus in view of the aforesaid discussion, the application is allowed.

Let necessary amendment in the memo of petition be carried out by the learned counsel for the petitioner within a period of one week .
2 WP-13043-2023 Learned counsel for the respondents are also at liberty to file the additional reply in view of the amendment made by the petitioner within a period of 6 weeks.
Let a copy of the amendment memo of petition be filed by learned counsel for the petitioner within a period of seven days by supplying a copy of the same to the learned counsel for the respondents.
